text:
Vegas arrives in St. Louis two days removed from a 6-2 loss to Tampa Bay at home that ended a three-game winning streak, with Parker Wotherspoon out. The Blues beat Winnipeg 2-1 in their last game and open game two of a five-game home stand without Ross Johnston, Dillon Dube and Alexey Toropchenko. Both teams are 3-2-0 in their last five, and this is their first meeting of the season; the Golden Knights won two of three last year.

The chance numbers are close. At five on five, Vegas has taken 53% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) and St. Louis 51%. The power play is where they split: Vegas generates 0.89 expected goals per game with the man advantage, St. Louis 0.54. The Blues' penalty kill allows 0.55 expected goals per game, against 0.3 for Vegas. In net, projected starter Carter Hart is at -1.07 goals saved above expected this season (how many goals he has stopped beyond what an average goalie would on the same shots). Projected starter Joel Hofer is at +2.83, after +11.05 last season.

For Vegas, Mark Stone has goals in three straight games and a 34% chance to score tonight, though he's flagged as due to cool. Mitch Marner brings a seven-game point streak. For St. Louis, Dylan Holloway is on a five-game point streak, and Mason McTavish is flagged as a breakout.
